label: A hand
caption: Each hand has 27 bones and about 17,000 touch receptors.
license: Pexels License (free to use; attribution not required)
notes: Bridge between the drone photo of the person (3.5 m) and skin-macro (2.3 cm), which was a 152x jump. Square crop (600,600)-(4000,4000) of the 4000x6000 original; scale from fingernail width (~1.2 cm) and hand length, about 0.06 mm/px -> 0.20 m. Rotated -30 deg so the fingers point the same way as the woman's hand in person.jpg. focus = skin on the back of the hand.

label: Skin
caption: The back of a hand: a landscape of ridges, furrows and fine hairs.
credit: Montavius Howard (TongCreator), via Pixabay / Wikimedia Commons
notes: Phone macro (LG G4). No scale bar: width estimated from the vellus hair (~5.7 px thick at 5312 px, assumed ~25 um => ~4.4 um/px => ~23 mm) cross-checked with skin-furrow polygon size (~1.5 mm). Uncertain by ~+/-40%. Focus: sharp furrow-crossing just below the root of the visible hair.

label: Skin surface
caption: Dry skin flakes: the outer layer is made of dead, flattened cells.
notes: Close-up photo of dry skin on the back of a hand. No scale bar: width estimated from furrow spacing (~350 px between primary furrows, taken as ~1 mm) => ~5.5 mm. Colour warmed slightly toward skin-macro. Focus on a flaky plateau beside a diagonal furrow (resembles the NCI SEM).

label: Skin (electron microscope)
caption: Under an electron microscope, skin looks like cracked, flaking terrain.
credit: Bruce Wetzel & Harry Schaefer, National Cancer Institute (NIH)
notes: SEM of human skin surface. 100 um scale bar = 359 px (measured) on 1800 px width => 501 um. Cropped bottom 99 px (scale bar/label). Focus on the steep diagonal skin ridge crest (upper right), which lines up with the hair shaft in hair-sem.

label: Human hair
caption: A single hair is armoured with overlapping scales called the cuticle.
credit: Nicola Angeli / MUSE - Museo delle Scienze, Trento (Wikimedia Commons)
notes: ZEISS SEM, 2000x. 10 um scale bar = 136 px on 2048 px => 150.6 um wide. Cropped to y<1240 to remove the data bar and the green in-image scale bar. The hair runs the same diagonal as the skin ridge in skin-sem. Focus on cuticle scale edges mid-shaft.

label: Bacteria
caption: Staphylococcus bacteria: millions live on your skin right now.
credit: CDC / Janice Carr, Deepak Mandhalapu (Public Health Image Library #7820)
notes: SEM 4780x of MRSA (Staphylococcus aureus). 5 um bar = 560 px on 2835 px => 25.3 um. Cropped data bar (y>=1670).

label: Staph cluster
caption: Staphylococcus grows in grape-like bunches; each ball is one cell.
credit: CDC / Matthew J. Arduino, DrPH (Public Health Image Library)
notes: Colorized SEM 20000x of VISA S. aureus. 1 um bar = 256 px on 1420 px => 5.55 um. Cropped data bar (y>=940).

label: Bacterium
caption: One bacterium is about a thousandth of a millimetre across.
credit: CDC / Matthew J. Arduino, DrPH (Public Health Image Library)
notes: Colorized SEM 50000x of the same VISA S. aureus sample. 500 nm bar = 317 px on 1420 px => 2.24 um. Cropped data bar (y>=945).

label: Bacteriophages
caption: Viruses that hunt bacteria latch on and inject their DNA.
notes: TEM (~200,000x) of phages attached to a bacterial cell wall. No scale bar: phage heads are ~95 px; taking a typical ~65 nm capsid gives ~0.68 nm/px => ~1.0 um wide (+/-30%).

label: T2 bacteriophage
caption: A virus is a protein shell packed with genes, plus a tail to inject them.
notes: Negative-stain TEM of phage T2. 100 nm bar = 646 px on 2021 px => 313 nm. Cropped the scale bar (y>=1870).

label: DNA
caption: DNA strands: 2 nm wide, yet each of your cells packs about 2 metres of it.
credit: Generated for this project (numpy sphere/volume renderer in assets/src/micro); coordinates from RCSB PDB 1BNA
license: CC0 (original render; PDB data is public domain)
notes: Render, 60 nm field (orthographic, exact). All-heavy-atom B-DNA, ~90k atoms, CPK space-filling, world-space AO + shadow map. Atomic coordinates: base pairs from PDB 1BNA (Drew et al. 1981, B-DNA dodecamer) placed along smooth 3D curves. Same scene/lighting as dna-helix and atoms, so the zoom nests exactly; focus = centre of the dna-helix view.

label: Double helix
caption: The double helix: two sugar-phosphate backbones twisted around paired bases.
credit: Generated for this project (numpy sphere/volume renderer in assets/src/micro); coordinates from RCSB PDB 1BNA
license: CC0 (original render; PDB data is public domain)
notes: Render, 8 nm field of the same scene as dna-strands (hero strand through the origin). Screw fitted from 1BNA: 35.4 deg/bp, 3.37 A rise. Focus = projected centre of the atoms view.

label: Atoms
caption: Each ball is one atom: carbon (grey), oxygen (red), nitrogen (blue), phosphorus (gold).
credit: Generated for this project (numpy sphere/volume renderer in assets/src/micro); coordinates from RCSB PDB 1BNA
license: CC0 (original render; PDB data is public domain)
notes: Render, 1.6 nm field of the same scene; spheres at van der Waals radii (C 1.70, N 1.55, O 1.52, P 1.80 A). Centred on a front-facing sugar carbon; focus = that carbon (becomes the atom level).

label: Carbon atom
caption: A carbon atom: six electrons in a fuzzy cloud around a nucleus 50,000x smaller.
credit: Generated for this project (numpy sphere/volume renderer in assets/src/micro)
notes: Generated. Projected electron density of ground-state carbon (1s2 2s2 2p2; hydrogen-like orbitals with Clementi-Raimondi effective charges), log tone-mapped so the glow fades at ~1.75 A (the vdW radius of the carbon sphere in 'atoms'). 0.6 nm field. Nucleus drawn as a tiny bright point (true size would be ~1/50,000 of the cloud). Black background for additive blending.

label: Nucleus
caption: The carbon nucleus: 6 protons and 6 neutrons carrying 99.97% of the atom's mass.
credit: Generated for this project (numpy sphere/volume renderer in assets/src/micro)
notes: Generated. Carbon-12: 12 nucleons (r = 0.86 fm) relaxed into a close-packed cluster, sphere renderer + bloom; protons warm red, neutrons grey-blue. 12 fm field (nucleus ~5.5 fm across). Focus = a front-facing proton.

label: Proton
caption: Inside a proton: three quarks bound by gluons, the strongest force in nature.
credit: Generated for this project (numpy sphere/volume renderer in assets/src/micro)
notes: Illustrative render (no real image exists). Fuzzy sphere of charge radius 0.84 fm, three valence quarks in the three colour charges joined by a Y-shaped gluon flux tube, faint sea-quark pairs. 3.6 fm field.
